task: Horizon 17 of agent-agnostic-browser-bridge: add byte-size caps to readConsoleMessages and readNetworkRequests, reusing horizon 16's shared oversize-result pattern.

analysis.objective: Extend horizon 16's shared non-throwing SizeCeilingOutcome/oversize-result pattern to readConsoleMessages and readNetworkRequests so a caller reading an oversized console or network capture window gets a structured, byte-measured 'too large' signal instead of an unbounded response body.
analysis.successDefinition: Done and correct means: (1) readConsoleMessages and readNetworkRequests each measure the serialised size of the CaptureReadResult they are about to return and, when it exceeds a defined byte/char ceiling, return a non-throwing structured oversize outcome built from the existing checkSizeLimit/buildOversizeResult helpers in tools/chrome-bridge/src/extension/size-limits.ts (reused as-is, not re-implemented) carrying actualBytes and limitBytes, exactly mirroring how executeScript/evaluatePage already behave; (2) a normal within-ceiling read is unaffected — same CaptureReadResult shape, same since/limit/nextSince/dropped/truncated semantics as today; (3) tools/chrome-bridge/src/mcp/server.ts's isOversizeResult/isError branch (currently scoped to executeScript/evaluatePage only, per the comment on line ~190) is extended to also cover readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests, so an oversize read surfaces as an MCP isError:true JSON text block, not a silently-huge success payload; (4) new/adjusted unit tests cover both the within-limit and over-limit paths for both tools (page-actions.unit.test.ts and server.unit.test.ts), and existing tests for the count-based `limit`/`since`/`nextSince`/`dropped`/`truncated` fields keep passing unchanged; (5) tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings 0, and vitest (unit-level, per .testguard.json placement) pass for tools/chrome-bridge; (6) README.md's readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests sections document the new byte-size ceiling and the too-large outcome shape, matching how executeScript/evaluatePage/captureTab are already documented.
assumptions: The byte ceiling for these two tools is a NEW constant (not a reuse of MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS/MAX_SCREENSHOT_BASE64_CHARS), sized for console/network payload shapes, and lives alongside the other size constants in page-actions.ts (or size-limits.ts) — the exact number is an implementation decision for Stage 2/3, not fixed here.

The measured size is the same convention already used elsewhere in this codebase: JSON.stringify(result).length (UTF-16 code units treated as a byte proxy), not a true UTF-8 byte count, since that is what executeScript/evaluatePage already do and no discovery entry says otherwise.

The oversize check applies to the whole CaptureReadResult (entries + metadata) after the existing count-based `limit` clamp already ran, not as a replacement for `limit`/`since` semantics — both mechanisms coexist, matching the two-lever precedent captureTab set (ladder AND flat ceiling exist for different tools).

'since' cursor and 'nextSince' bookkeeping remain unchanged by this horizon: an oversize result does not need to invent a partial-read/resume story now — a caller can retry with a smaller `limit` param, which is already supported.

No change to the extension-side ring buffer capacity, eviction, or per-entry truncation (MAX_CONSOLE_TEXT_BYTES / MAX_BODY_PREVIEW_BYTES already bound individual entries) — this horizon caps the aggregate serialised RESULT size, not per-entry content.

This horizon does not touch the dead active-tab code removal or any other deferred item listed in next-horizon-brief.md's 'Decisions the next horizon cannot avoid' — the user's scoping choice already excluded that alternative.
risks: The existing count-based `limit` (MAX_READ_LIMIT=500) may already keep most real-world results well under any reasonable byte ceiling, making the new guard rarely exercised in practice — live-Chrome verification (this project's binding pattern per decisions.md 2026-09-03) is needed to confirm the ceiling is reachable and the oversize path is real, not dead code.

Choosing the ceiling value without a live measurement (as horizon 13 initially did for captureTab, then had to replan after measuring real bytes) risks setting it too low (false positives on legitimate large-but-useful reads) or too high (never fires) — Stage 2/3 should measure a real large console/network buffer before fixing the number, mirroring horizon 13's replan lesson already recorded in decisions.md.

Extending the mcp/server.ts isOversizeResult branch to two more tool names is a small, mechanical change, but the existing code comment explicitly says the check is 'Scoped to these two tools only' — that comment must be updated in the same change or it becomes stale/misleading documentation.

If readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests results are large primarily because of MANY entries rather than a few huge ones, an aggregate oversize outcome could discard an entire otherwise-useful batch instead of degrading gracefully (e.g. returning fewer entries) — this mirrors the flat-ceiling (all-or-nothing) tradeoff decisions.md already accepted for executeScript/evaluatePage, so it is a known and accepted pattern, not a new risk to solve differently, but worth naming so it isn't assumed away.

No security/correctness invariant is being dropped by this task's scope as stated — it strictly adds a bound where none existed, so there is no conflict to flag against a caller-supplied acceptance criterion (none was supplied).
outOfScope: Removing the dead active-tab code surface (queryActiveTab/captureVisibleTab/NO_ACTIVE_TAB/activeTab permission) — this was the explicitly-rejected alternative in this horizon's AskUserQuestion round, not folded into this scope.

Any change to the count-based `since`/`limit`/`nextSince`/`dropped`/`truncated` cursor semantics of the ring-buffer read protocol (decisions.md 2026-09-02 horizon 2) — this horizon adds a byte guard alongside them, it does not redesign the read protocol.
Per-entry content truncation changes (MAX_CONSOLE_TEXT_BYTES, MAX_BODY_PREVIEW_BYTES) — those already bound individual entries and are untouched.

Any downscale/retry-ladder behavior for oversize reads (e.g. auto-retrying with a smaller `limit`) — the established precedent for executeScript/evaluatePage is a flat non-retrying ceiling, and readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests follow the same flat pattern, not captureTab's ladder.
Streaming/observation-frame delivery of console/network entries — the wire protocol's unused `observation` frame stays unused (decisions.md 2026-09-02 horizon 2); this horizon stays pull-only.

Persistent-CDP-session redesign, JPEG/quality downscale rungs for captureTab, or a second render-primitive consumer — these are other deferred items from next-horizon-brief.md's decision list that belong to different horizons.
Changes to boky's own extension/bridge/nest-host code — this project never touches boky itself (decisions.md 2026-09-02 horizon 1).
analysis.domainShapeReason: The objective is entirely about a subsystem's size-guard/error-signaling mechanism (an MCP tool response pipeline) rather than any business domain concept — it is infrastructure/pipeline vocabulary through and through.

discoveryFindings.finding: Both actions are implemented by a single shared closure `readCapture(channel)` inside `pageActionHandlers` (page-actions.ts). It validates `since`/`limit` via `resolveSince`/`resolveReadLimit`, resolves the sandbox tabId, then calls `captureStore.readConsole(tabId, { since, limit })` or `captureStore.readNetwork(...)` and returns `{ result }` verbatim -- there is no byte-size measurement or branching in this closure at all today, only count-based `limit`.
discoveryFindings.implication: The byte-size cap logic must be added inside (or wrapping) `readCapture`, after the store read returns `CaptureRead<T>` and before `{ result }` is returned -- it cannot reuse `coerceExecuteScriptOutcome`'s single-JSON-string check as-is since the payload here is an array of entries, not one JSON string.

discoveryFindings.finding: `CaptureRead<T>` = `{ entries: ReadonlyArray<T & {seq:number}>, nextSince: number, dropped: boolean, truncated: boolean }`. `truncated` is already defined as 'strictly more entries matched than were returned' (count-based, set inside `createCaptureRing.read()`), and `dropped` means the ring overwrote entries the caller's `since` never covered. There is no byte-size field anywhere in this type today.
discoveryFindings.implication: Reusing the existing `truncated` boolean for a byte-cap would overload its established meaning (count truncation) with a second, unrelated meaning (byte truncation). The plan should add a new field (e.g. via the oversize-result pattern, or a sibling flag) rather than repurpose `truncated`/`dropped`, to avoid breaking the CaptureRead contract's existing unit tests and docs.

discoveryFindings.area: size-limits.ts exact API this horizon must reuse
discoveryFindings.finding: `checkSizeLimit(actualBytes, limitBytes): SizeCeilingOutcome` is a pure comparison (`withinLimit = actualBytes <= limitBytes`, inclusive). `buildOversizeResult(outcome): OversizeResult` maps it to `{ tooLarge: boolean, actualBytes: number, limitBytes: number }`. Both are already tool-agnostic per their doc comments ('or any future tool that returns a serialised value'). `executeScript`/`evaluatePage` call this via `coerceExecuteScriptOutcome`: measure `json.length`, `checkSizeLimit(json.length, MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS)`, and on `!withinLimit` return `{ result: buildOversizeResult(ceiling) }` INSTEAD of the normal `{ value }` result -- i.e. the oversize result today fully replaces the payload, it does not accompany a partial one.
discoveryFindings.implication: For readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests, a design decision is needed: whether an oversize read total-replaces the whole `CaptureRead` payload (matching executeScript/evaluatePage's contract exactly, but breaking the read tools' 'always return partial entries + cursor' UX) or whether the byte cap instead trims the entries array before hitting the ceiling (more useful, but not literally 'reuse the pattern' the same way). The task text says 'reuse... do not reimplement' the pattern, so the safest reading is: measure the serialized entries size, and only fall back to `buildOversizeResult` as a full-replace sentinel when even the smallest read (or a single entry) cannot fit -- but this needs to be resolved explicitly in the plan, not assumed.

discoveryFindings.finding: The oversize branch is explicitly gated by `if (toolName === "executeScript" || toolName === "evaluatePage")` (line 184) wrapping `isOversizeResult(response.result)`, with a comment: 'Scoped to these two tools only -- the check never runs for captureTab/findElement/read tools.' `isOversizeResult` itself is a generic structural check (`tooLarge === true` + numeric `actualBytes`/`limitBytes`) with no tool-name awareness -- the scoping lives entirely in the `toolName ===` condition.
discoveryFindings.implication: This horizon must literally widen that string check to `toolName === "executeScript" || toolName === "evaluatePage" || toolName === "readConsoleMessages" || toolName === "readNetworkRequests"` (or equivalent), update the comment (it currently explicitly disclaims read tools), and update the existing unit test 'does not flag a tooLarge-shaped result on a tool outside executeScript/evaluatePage' at src/mcp/server.unit.test.ts:258 which currently uses `getPageText` as its 'outside' example -- that test's premise is unaffected (getPageText stays outside), but a new sibling test proving readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests ARE now inside the branch is needed.

discoveryFindings.area: tool-catalog.ts entries for the two read tools
discoveryFindings.finding: `readConsoleMessages`/`readNetworkRequests` catalog entries (tool-catalog.ts lines 250-267) have descriptions mentioning only `since`/`nextSince` cursor semantics and per-tab in-memory lifetime; input schema is `{ properties: { ...SINCE_LIMIT_PROPERTIES }, additionalProperties: false }` with no byte-size-related property. `SINCE_LIMIT_PROPERTIES` (line 50) documents `since`/`limit` only. executeScript/evaluatePage's descriptions explicitly mention 'an over-large result comes back as an error, not a value' as one line appended to their descriptions.
discoveryFindings.implication: The two read-tool descriptions should get an added sentence documenting the new byte cap and the too-large behavior, matching the executeScript/evaluatePage phrasing convention, but likely no new input-schema property is needed since this is a response-shaping cap, not a caller-tunable input (mirrors executeScript/evaluatePage, which also added no new input param for their cap).

discoveryFindings.area: README.md documentation convention for oversize/too-large behavior
discoveryFindings.finding: README.md has a dedicated '### Screenshot size policy' section for captureTab's downscale ladder, and a paragraph under '### readConsoleMessages / readNetworkRequests' documenting executeScript/evaluatePage's over-large JSON-char cap with the exact isError/{tooLarge,actualBytes,limitBytes} shape (lines 165-181). The read-tools' own paragraph further down (lines 274-292) documents `since`/`limit`/`entries`/`nextSince`/`dropped`/`truncated` plus 'Buffer caps... DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES=500, MAX_CONSOLE_TEXT_BYTES=8192, MAX_BODY_PREVIEW_BYTES=4096' but currently says nothing about a per-read byte ceiling.
discoveryFindings.implication: The plan should extend the existing read-tools paragraph (not create a new section) to document the new byte cap constant, its value, and the resulting isError/too-large shape, following the same terse convention already used for executeScript/evaluatePage in that same section.

discoveryFindings.area: Existing unit test coverage for read tools' size/limit behavior
discoveryFindings.finding: page-actions.unit.test.ts's 'pageActionHandlers -- readConsoleMessages / readNetworkRequests' describe block (lines 2505-2643) covers: since/limit forwarding to the right store method, limit clamping to MAX_READ_LIMIT, bad since/limit rejection, sandbox-tab-resolution failure, a throwing store surfaced via guard, and stale/equal cursor behavior. None of these tests touch byte size at all -- there is currently zero test coverage of a byte cap for these two tools (because the cap does not exist yet). server.unit.test.ts's oversize describe block (lines ~214-269) has tests only for executeScript/evaluatePage plus one 'outside the branch' test using getPageText.
discoveryFindings.implication: This is purely additive test work: new unit tests are needed in page-actions.unit.test.ts for the new byte-measuring/oversize-branching logic in `readCapture`, and new/updated tests in server.unit.test.ts proving readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests are now inside the isError/isOversizeResult branch. No existing test asserts an uncapped/no-limit invariant that would need to be deleted, aside from the general shape assertions (e.g. the exact-equality check at line 2639-2641) which must keep passing for normal-size reads.

discoveryFindings.area: Existing byte-size constants available for reuse
discoveryFindings.finding: page-actions.ts already defines `MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS = 1_000_000` and `MAX_SCREENSHOT_BASE64_CHARS = 1_200_000`, both scoped by their own doc comments to their specific tool (the doc comment for MAX_SCREENSHOT_BASE64_CHARS explicitly says 'Sibling to MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS, scoped to the screenshot result -- a cross-tool cap is a separate open question'). Separately, protocol/capture.ts defines `MAX_CONSOLE_TEXT_BYTES = 8192` (per-entry console text cap) and `MAX_BODY_PREVIEW_BYTES = 4096` (per-entry network body-preview cap) -- both are PER-ENTRY truncation caps applied in capture-store.ts's `reboundConsole`/`reboundNetwork` at ingest time, not per-READ (whole-page) caps.
discoveryFindings.implication: None of the existing constants are directly reusable as a whole-response byte ceiling for a page of console/network entries -- a NEW constant (e.g. MAX_CONSOLE_READ_RESULT_BYTES / MAX_NETWORK_READ_RESULT_BYTES, or one shared MAX_CAPTURE_READ_RESULT_BYTES) is needed, following the same co-located, doc-commented convention as the other two.

discoveryFindings.area: Ring buffer / capture store measurement point
discoveryFindings.finding: `createCaptureRing.read()` (capture-buffer.ts) already slices `matched` down to `limit` entries and computes `truncated` purely by count, with no serialization or byte measurement anywhere in the ring. `CaptureStore.readConsole`/`readNetwork` (capture-store.ts) just delegate straight to `rings.console.read(query)` / `rings.network.read(query)` with no post-processing. There is no natural existing seam where a serialized-size measurement happens before the count clamp -- the count clamp happens first and is unconditional.
discoveryFindings.implication: Byte-size measurement should happen AFTER the count-based `.read()` returns (i.e. in `readCapture` in page-actions.ts, or as a new thin wrapper step in capture-store.ts), by JSON-stringifying the returned `entries` array (or summing serialized per-entry lengths) and comparing against the new constant via `checkSizeLimit`. Changing the ring buffer itself is not required and would entangle an unrelated, already-tested layer; keeping the byte check downstream of the ring (in the read-tool handler, mirroring where executeScript/evaluatePage do their check) is the lower-risk, most-reuse-consistent location.

requiredMaterials.name: Live Chrome session with the extension loaded and nest-host relay running
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: To pick real MAX_CONSOLE_READ_RESULT_BYTES / MAX_NETWORK_READ_RESULT_BYTES ceiling values with confidence, a real-world serialized size for a full (or near-MAX_READ_LIMIT) console/network capture window must be measured, not guessed. stage1-analysis.json's risks section explicitly calls this out: setting the ceiling without a live measurement risks the same problem horizon 13 hit with captureTab (had to replan after measuring real bytes), and confirms whether the count-based limit=500 already keeps results well under any reasonable byte ceiling (which would make the new guard rarely/never exercised).
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Start the relay + workflow engine from the repo root (`npm start`), load tools/chrome-bridge's extension unpacked in a real Chrome profile, open a page that generates a substantial console/network volume, then use the devtools bridge (ext_command / chrome-bridge MCP tools, e.g. readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests with a large `limit`) to capture and JSON.stringify-measure a realistic entries payload before fixing the two new byte constants.

phases.name: Measure real console and network read sizes
phases.goal: Using a live Chrome session with the extension loaded and the nest-host relay running, capture a near-MAX_READ_LIMIT (500-entry) console read and network read from a page that produces heavy console/network volume, JSON.stringify the returned `entries` array for each, and record the measured character counts so the next phase can fix real byte-ceiling constants instead of guessed ones.
phases.rationale: stage1-analysis.json's risks section and this project's binding decisions.md precedent (horizon 13 had to replan captureTab after guessing a ceiling) both require a real measurement before any byte-size constant is written into code — this phase produces that evidence.
changes: Start the relay + workflow engine (`npm start` from repo root) and load tools/chrome-bridge's extension unpacked in Chrome
Navigate the sandbox tab to a page that generates substantial console output and network traffic (e.g. a console-heavy demo page or a network-heavy site)
Via the devtools/chrome-bridge MCP tools, call readConsoleMessages and readNetworkRequests with limit=500 (the existing MAX_READ_LIMIT) against that page

JSON.stringify the returned `entries` array for each response and record its `.length` alongside the entry count and per-entry cap context (MAX_CONSOLE_TEXT_BYTES=8192, MAX_BODY_PREVIEW_BYTES=4096) as the evidence the next phase's constants are grounded on

Append one binding-decision line to docs/roadmaps/agent-agnostic-browser-bridge/decisions.md (following the file's existing `- YYYY-MM-DD | horizon N | <decision> — because <reason>` convention, at most 240 chars) recording the measured console and network character counts as the grounding fact for the next phase's byte-ceiling constants
inputs: Live Chrome session with the extension loaded and nest-host relay running (required material)
MAX_READ_LIMIT / per-entry cap constants already in page-actions.ts and protocol/capture.ts
phases.expectedResult: A recorded measurement (character-length of JSON.stringify(entries) for a 500-entry console read and a 500-entry network read against a real page), landed as a one-line binding-decision entry in docs/roadmaps/agent-agnostic-browser-bridge/decisions.md, that the next phase cites when choosing MAX_CONSOLE_READ_RESULT_CHARS / MAX_NETWORK_READ_RESULT_CHARS.

rubric.label: Both read-type measurements recorded at near-MAX_READ_LIMIT scale
rubric.ruleStatement: decisions.md must carry a new line stating the measured JSON.stringify(entries).length for BOTH a console read and a network read, each captured with limit=500 against a page producing genuinely heavy volume; 10 means both counts are exact figures with entry counts stated and both entry counts are at or near 500, 8 is the expected competent result (both figures present, entry counts clearly above 400), and a plausible careful attempt still misses the bar if it captures a quiet page.
passCriteria: decisions.md contains a newly appended line (not an edit to an existing line) with two distinct numeric character-count figures, one clearly labeled console and one clearly labeled network
the line or its immediate context states the entry count returned for each read (not just the character count)
both stated entry counts are at least 400 (near the 500-entry MAX_READ_LIMIT), confirming the page actually produced heavy volume rather than a handful of log lines
failureExamples: the line reports only the network figure and omits console entirely, leaving half the grounding fact missing

a careful developer tests against a mostly-idle page and honestly records real numbers, but entry counts come back at 15 console / 40 network — technically real evidence but useless for grounding a near-500-entry ceiling

rubric.label: Measurement is tied to the existing per-entry byte caps
rubric.ruleStatement: the decision line or its evidence must reference the per-entry caps already active during measurement (MAX_CONSOLE_TEXT_BYTES=8192, MAX_BODY_PREVIEW_BYTES=4096) so the next phase can reason about entries-times-caps rather than an opaque total; 10 means both cap names and values are cited and match the source constants exactly, 8 is citing both caps by name even if values are paraphrased, and a failure is recording totals with no mention of what per-entry truncation, if any, was in effect.
passCriteria: the decisions.md line or accompanying evidence names at least one of MAX_CONSOLE_TEXT_BYTES / MAX_BODY_PREVIEW_BYTES
any numeric value cited for those caps matches the actual constant value in tools/chrome-bridge/src/extension/page-actions.ts or protocol/capture.ts at the time of measurement
failureExamples: the line states '512340 chars for console, 398120 for network' with no mention of the per-entry text/body caps, so the next phase cannot tell whether entries were already truncated during measurement
a developer cites MAX_CONSOLE_TEXT_BYTES from memory as 4096 instead of the actual 8192 value in source, silently corrupting the grounding fact

rubric.label: Phase stays measurement-only; no ceiling constants or wiring added yet
rubric.ruleStatement: this phase's file changes must be limited to decisions.md (plus any read-only evidence artifacts); readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests bodies and size-limits.ts must be untouched, since defining MAX_CONSOLE_READ_RESULT_CHARS/MAX_NETWORK_READ_RESULT_CHARS and wiring SizeCeilingOutcome is the next phase's job. 10 means the diff touches only decisions.md, 8 means no production logic changed even if a throwaway measurement script was added and removed, and a failure is any new ceiling constant or checkSizeLimit/buildOversizeResult call landing in page-actions.ts during this phase.
passCriteria: git diff for this phase's commit(s) shows no new constant definitions (e.g. MAX_CONSOLE_READ_RESULT_CHARS, MAX_NETWORK_READ_RESULT_CHARS) in page-actions.ts or size-limits.ts
readConsoleMessages and readNetworkRequests function bodies in page-actions.ts are byte-for-byte unchanged from before this phase
no new checkSizeLimit/buildOversizeResult call sites appear for console or network reads
failureExamples: a developer eager to finish in one pass adds the two new MAX_*_READ_RESULT_CHARS constants and wires checkSizeLimit into both readers in the same commit as the decisions.md line, collapsing the measurement and fix phases together
the diff adds a temporary console.log-based measurement helper directly inside readNetworkRequests and leaves it in place instead of removing it after capturing the numbers

rubric.label: Numbers are traceable to a real live-session capture, not estimated
rubric.ruleStatement: the decisions.md entry or its evidence must make clear the figures came from actually invoking readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests with limit=500 against a real Chrome session via the live bridge, on an identifiable page with heavy volume; 10 means the method, limit, and source page are all named, 8 means at least the method and limit are stated, and a failure is presenting numbers with no way to tell how or against what they were produced.
passCriteria: decisions.md text or a referenced evidence note names the tool calls used (readConsoleMessages / readNetworkRequests) and states limit=500
the page or site used to generate console/network volume is named or described (e.g. a specific URL or a description of what made it heavy), not left implicit
failureExamples: the line states two character counts with no indication of what page, tool call, or limit produced them, making the figures unreproducible and unverifiable by the next phase's author
a developer estimates the numbers by reasoning about entry-count times per-entry cap instead of actually driving the live session, then records them as if measured

rubric.label: Appended line matches decisions.md's existing convention
rubric.ruleStatement: the new line must match the file's established single-line, ≤240-char, dated-entry format used by prior binding decisions (e.g. the horizon 13 captureTab precedent); 10 means it is indistinguishable in style from surrounding entries and exactly conforms to the 240-char cap, 8 means it is a single line under the cap but formatted slightly differently from neighbors, and a failure is a multi-line note or missing the file's structural convention.
passCriteria: the new entry is a single line, not a multi-line paragraph or new subsection
the line is at most 240 characters
the line's prefix/structure (date or id marker, phrasing style) visually matches at least two neighboring existing entries in the file
failureExamples: the developer appends a short paragraph with a header instead of one bullet-style line, breaking the file's scanability even though the content is accurate and well-cited
the line is technically one line but 280 characters long, exceeding the file's stated 240-char convention

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is scope creep — while capturing evidence it's tempting to also add MAX_CONSOLE_READ_RESULT_CHARS/MAX_NETWORK_READ_RESULT_CHARS and wire checkSizeLimit into the readers in the same pass; fix by reverting all page-actions.ts/size-limits.ts changes and keeping this phase's diff to the single decisions.md line.

phases.name: Add byte-size ceiling to console and network reads
phases.goal: Add new, measurement-grounded byte-size constants for readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests and make the shared `readCapture` closure in page-actions.ts measure the serialised size of the entries it is about to return, replacing the whole result with `buildOversizeResult` (via the existing `checkSizeLimit`/`buildOversizeResult` helpers from size-limits.ts) when it exceeds the ceiling — exactly mirroring how `coerceExecuteScriptOutcome` already handles executeScript's oversize case.
phases.rationale: Today `readCapture` (page-actions.ts) has no byte-size check at all, only the count-based `limit`/`since` clamp — an unbounded console/network read can return an arbitrarily large payload. size-limits.ts's helpers are already tool-agnostic per their doc comments and must be reused as-is, not re-implemented, per the horizon's explicit constraint.
changes: Add MAX_CONSOLE_READ_RESULT_CHARS and MAX_NETWORK_READ_RESULT_CHARS constants near MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS/MAX_SCREENSHOT_BASE64_CHARS, each with a doc comment stating the measured basis from the prior phase and that it bounds the whole serialised CaptureRead result, not a per-entry value

In the `readCapture(channel)` closure, after `captureStore.readConsole`/`readNetwork` returns its CaptureRead, JSON.stringify the result, run it through `checkSizeLimit(json.length, ceilingForChannel)`, and on `!withinLimit` return `{ result: buildOversizeResult(ceiling) }` instead of `{ result }` — leaving the count-based `limit`/`since`/`nextSince`/`dropped`/`truncated` clamp that already ran untouched

Add unit tests in page-actions.unit.test.ts covering: an under-cap read for both channels returns the normal CaptureReadResult unchanged, and an over-cap read for both channels returns the OversizeResult shape instead
inputs: Measured character counts from the live-Chrome measurement phase
coerceExecuteScriptOutcome's existing oversize branch (page-actions.ts) as the pattern to mirror
phases.expectedResult: readCapture returns a structured OversizeResult (in place of the normal CaptureReadResult) for both readConsoleMessages and readNetworkRequests when the serialised result exceeds its new byte ceiling, covered by new unit tests, with the existing count-based limit/since tests unaffected.

rubric.label: Oversize check reuses size-limits.ts helpers verbatim
rubric.ruleStatement: readCapture's oversize branch must call the existing checkSizeLimit/buildOversizeResult exports from size-limits.ts with no new comparison, threshold math, or duplicate OversizeResult-shaping logic written in page-actions.ts. 10 means the branch is a one-to-one structural mirror of coerceExecuteScriptOutcome's existing oversize branch (same call shape, same two-line pattern); 8 is the expected score for a correct call to both helpers that achieves the same effect with minor stylistic divergence (e.g. an extra local variable); a diff introducing any manual `>` / `.length >` comparison against a ceiling constant, or a hand-built `{ tooLarge, actualBytes, limitBytes }` object literal anywhere in page-actions.ts, fails this dimension outright.
passCriteria: grep page-actions.ts for the new oversize branch and confirm it calls `checkSizeLimit(...)` and passes the result to `buildOversizeResult(...)`, not a hand-rolled comparison
confirm no new object literal with keys `tooLarge`/`actualBytes`/`limitBytes` is constructed anywhere outside size-limits.ts
confirm size-limits.ts itself is unmodified in the diff (git diff shows no changes to that file)
failureExamples: a developer writes `if (json.length > MAX_CONSOLE_READ_RESULT_CHARS) return { result: { tooLarge: true, actualBytes: json.length, limitBytes: MAX_CONSOLE_READ_RESULT_CHARS } }` instead of calling checkSizeLimit/buildOversizeResult — functionally equivalent but duplicates policy the phase explicitly says must be reused as-is
checkSizeLimit is called but its SizeCeilingOutcome is manually destructured and re-assembled into a differently-shaped object instead of being passed straight to buildOversizeResult

rubric.label: Both readConsoleMessages and readNetworkRequests get the ceiling
rubric.ruleStatement: The size check must run for both the 'console' and 'network' branches of the shared readCapture closure, each measured against its own distinct constant (MAX_CONSOLE_READ_RESULT_CHARS vs MAX_NETWORK_READ_RESULT_CHARS), not a single shared ceiling applied to both channels. 10 means both channels are unmistakably wired to their own named constant and this is visible from a single read of the closure; 8 is the expected score when both channels are correctly gated even if the ceiling-selection logic is a plain ternary rather than something more elegant; a diff that adds the check for only one channel, or that applies one constant to both channels, fails.
passCriteria: grep for MAX_CONSOLE_READ_RESULT_CHARS and MAX_NETWORK_READ_RESULT_CHARS in page-actions.ts and confirm each name appears exactly once as the ceiling argument used by its matching channel inside readCapture

successCriteria: Done and correct means: (1) readConsoleMessages and readNetworkRequests each measure the serialised size of the CaptureReadResult they are about to return and, when it exceeds a defined byte/char ceiling, return a non-throwing structured oversize outcome built from the existing checkSizeLimit/buildOversizeResult helpers in tools/chrome-bridge/src/extension/size-limits.ts (reused as-is, not re-implemented) carrying actualBytes and limitBytes, exactly mirroring how executeScript/evaluatePage already behave; (2) a normal within-ceiling read is unaffected — same CaptureReadResult shape, same since/limit/nextSince/dropped/truncated semantics as today; (3) tools/chrome-bridge/src/mcp/server.ts's isOversizeResult/isError branch (currently scoped to executeScript/evaluatePage only, per the comment on line ~190) is extended to also cover readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests, so an oversize read surfaces as an MCP isError:true JSON text block, not a silently-huge success payload; (4) new/adjusted unit tests cover both the within-limit and over-limit paths for both tools (page-actions.unit.test.ts and server.unit.test.ts), and existing tests for the count-based `limit`/`since`/`nextSince`/`dropped`/`truncated` fields keep passing unchanged; (5) tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings 0, and vitest (unit-level, per .testguard.json placement) pass for tools/chrome-bridge; (6) README.md's readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests sections document the new byte-size ceiling and the too-large outcome shape, matching how executeScript/evaluatePage/captureTab are already documented.

Add byte-size ceiling to console and network reads: readCapture returns a structured OversizeResult (in place of the normal CaptureReadResult) for both readConsoleMessages and readNetworkRequests when the serialised result exceeds its new byte ceiling, covered by new unit tests, with the existing count-based limit/since tests unaffected.

Flag oversize console/network reads as MCP errors: mcp/server.ts's isError/isOversizeResult branch covers readConsoleMessages and readNetworkRequests (comment updated to match), verified by new unit tests.

Document the read-tool size cap in catalog and README: tool-catalog.ts's readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests descriptions (verified by a tool-catalog.unit.test.ts assertion) and README.md's readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests section both document the new byte-size ceiling and the too-large/isError behavior.
deferred: Trimming the entries array down to fit under the byte ceiling instead of wholesale-replacing the result with OversizeResult — Fails the YAGNI 'simplest thing that could work' gate for this horizon: the task explicitly requires reusing the horizon-16 pattern exactly (full-replace sentinel), and any partial-trim/pagination behavior would be a new, unrequested read-protocol feature layered on top of the existing since/limit/nextSince cursor — out of scope per stage1-analysis.json's outOfScope list.

A single shared MAX_CAPTURE_READ_RESULT_CHARS constant instead of separate console/network constants — Deferred pending the live measurement in phase 0 — console and network payload shapes differ enough (text-heavy vs. URL/status/body-preview-heavy) that collapsing them into one constant before measuring both would be guessing ahead of evidence; if measurement shows near-identical real-world sizes, a future horizon can consolidate them, but doing so speculatively now fails the 'don't build for an imagined future need' gate.

Removing the dead active-tab code surface (queryActiveTab/captureVisibleTab/NO_ACTIVE_TAB/activeTab permission) — Explicitly out of scope per stage1-analysis.json — a previously-rejected alternative from a different horizon's scoping round, unrelated to this task's byte-cap objective.

Any pagination/continuation retrieval mechanism for an oversize read (e.g. auto-retry with a smaller limit) — Explicitly out of scope per stage1-analysis.json — the established flat, non-retrying ceiling precedent from executeScript/evaluatePage is what this horizon must mirror, not captureTab's ladder/retry behavior.

Any change to the count-based `since`/`limit`/`nextSince`/`dropped`/`truncated` cursor semantics of the ring-buffer read protocol (decisions.md 2026-09-02 horizon 2) — this horizon adds a byte guard alongside them, it does not redesign the read protocol.
Per-entry content truncation changes (MAX_CONSOLE_TEXT_BYTES, MAX_BODY_PREVIEW_BYTES) — those already bound individual entries and are untouched.

Any downscale/retry-ladder behavior for oversize reads (e.g. auto-retrying with a smaller `limit`) — the established precedent for executeScript/evaluatePage is a flat non-retrying ceiling, and readConsoleMessages/readNetworkRequests follow the same flat pattern, not captureTab's ladder.
Streaming/observation-frame delivery of console/network entries — the wire protocol's unused `observation` frame stays unused (decisions.md 2026-09-02 horizon 2); this horizon stays pull-only.

Persistent-CDP-session redesign, JPEG/quality downscale rungs for captureTab, or a second render-primitive consumer — these are other deferred items from next-horizon-brief.md's decision list that belong to different horizons.
Changes to boky's own extension/bridge/nest-host code — this project never touches boky itself (decisions.md 2026-09-02 horizon 1).
